CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left shoulder pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mrs. Anderson is a 44-year-old female presenting with left shoulder pain that began one week ago. The pain started during a gymnastics class when the patient fell into an awkward position during a move. The patient denies having taken any pain medications initially but did try Tylenol for two to three days without relief. She reports that any movement of the left shoulder causes pain. X-ray imaging was obtained and does not reveal any fracture or broken bone, suggesting a joint injury.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports pain with all movements of the left shoulder. Pain is exacerbated with both forward and backward movement of the shoulder.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
History of surgery on the left arm.

MEDICATIONS
Tylenol (taken for two to three days without significant relief).

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient participates in gymnastics classes.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Left shoulder demonstrates pain with active range of motion in all directions, including forward and backward movement.

RESULTS
Left shoulder X-ray: No evidence of fracture or broken bone.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Left shoulder joint injury. Patient advised to rest the left arm for 3-4 weeks and avoid carrying heavy weights. Recommended ibuprofen 600 mg three times daily for one week. Patient may also use ice or heat pad for pain relief. Alternative pain relief options discussed include Advil or Aleve. Patient instructed to follow up in three weeks; if pain persists, further imaging may be considered at that time. Patient may contact office earlier if pain worsens or does not improve.
